name: Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd
title: Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd - 544407 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Aegis Vopak is scaling storage ahead of demand: liquid capacity up 3.75x and a ~USD5bn capex plan to 2030, with JNPT's 318,100 cbm expansion starting next month and FY26 revenue up 17% to INR923.1 crores.

summary.headline: Aegis Vopak FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR923.1 crores and net profit 52.1% to INR341.9 crores; Q4 revenue up 22.2% to INR243.5 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's first full year as a listed entity, with revenue from operations up 17% YoY to INR923.1 crores and operating EBITDA up 19.4% to INR686.5 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR243.5 crores, with Q4 operating EBITDA up 24.2% to INR179.2 crores and net profit up 15.3% to INR73.9 crores. Management said FY25 and FY26 figures were restated to consolidate Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited, which was acquired as a 75% stake in Haldia. Management reiterated a 30-40% YoY throughput growth target for FY27 and a long-term capex roadmap of about USD5 billion by 2030.

financial_highlights.value: INR0.2 per share (about 2.0% on INR10 face value)

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR440.5 crores (+27.8% YoY); Q4 INR121.1 crores (+31% YoY) on volumes, capacity additions and product mix. Management cites about INR3,000 per CBM as a good blended earning.

segments.name: Gas terminaling (LPG)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR482.6 crores (+8.6% YoY); Q4 INR122.4 crores (+14.6% YoY). Gas throughput rose to 3.9 million tons in FY26 from 3.3 million tons in FY25.

segments.name: Ammonia (emerging)
segments.commentary: Pipavav ammonia terminal of 36,000 metric tons static capacity, backed by a 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc; commissioning expected next month per management. Not yet a reported revenue line.

guidance_outlook: FY27 throughput growth of 30-40% YoY, which management says is its standing target (not formal guidance).
FY27 capex of USD1.2 billion, cumulative aggregate capex reaching about USD1.2 billion by end of next year.
FY28 capex expected to be close to INR5,000 crores; numbers to be finalised.
JNPT liquid expansion (318,100 CBM) mostly operational in H1 FY27, with full completion targeted by around October; contributes from Q2 FY27.
Long-term capex pipeline of about USD5 billion by 2030, with a gearing target of about 0.6x and a planned second-phase QIP (equity).
capex_capacity: JNPT: liquid storage of 106,900 CBM today; expansion adds about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total capex about INR1,675 crores; phase 1 targeted for Q1 FY27.

Kandla: about 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; CRL4 liquid terminal adds 94,148 CBM, on track for commissioning next year (FY27). Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. VLGC-compliant after first VLGC received in December 2025.

Pipavav: cryogenic LPG terminal of 48,000 MT commissioned June 2025 (total LPG 70,800 MT); new VLGC-compliant jetty expected to complete within calendar 2026; 15-year take-or-pay for 0.5 million MT per year of petroleum products with operations expected by year-end; ammonia terminal of 36,000 MT.

Mangalore: cryogenic LPG terminal of 82,000 MT commissioned June 2025; 75,000 CBM liquid added and operational, total liquid 193,000 CBM; LPG rail gantry under construction; land secured for a further 60,000 CBM.

Haldia: 226,890 CBM liquid storage; about 25,000 MT LPG added via 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG under a HPCL exclusive terminaling agreement through 2038; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion. Kochi: about 82,545 CBM, with up to 60,000 CBM planned on newly allotted land.
demand_pricing: Management says the company operates as an open-access terminal and does not track revenue split between long-term and spot contracts; long-term contracts exist but are not the norm. Operates close to 25 units across India.

LPG imports were hit after Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption from March; volumes were down about 50% in March, improving to a 30-35% shortfall in May. Parent's distribution volumes grew strongly in Q4, supporting terminal utilisation.
Management expects the JNPT expansion to earn full realisations from commissioning, as JNPT has more demand, rather than ramping up gradually.
Liquid terminals are paid on capacity hired, so management measures earnings per CBM rather than physical occupancy.
Business mix expected to shift toward gas, at about 55:45 or 60:40 gas to liquid over the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity being built by Aegis Vopak directly or by Aegis Logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Land is leased to Aegis Vopak, but the parent Aegis Logistics builds the infrastructure under its supervision, for cost and in-house capability reasons; Aegis Vopak then owns and operates the terminals.

qa_highlights.question: What supports a USD5 billion capex plan when only USD1.2 billion has been spent so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex grew from USD200 million to USD600 million to USD1.2 billion, and is now running at INR4,000-5,000 crores a year, rising later. Spending follows demand, with larger projects in the last two years of the period, funded by EBITDA growth and a second-phase QIP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix by customer and contract term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track these statistics; it runs as an open-access terminal with no product or customer dependence, and long-term contracts exist but are not the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Lease expiries and business mix over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Most leases are not near expiry; the only near-term one is Pipavav's concessionaire lease in 2029. Gas is expected to be more dominant, at about 55:45 or 60:40 gas to liquid.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance and FY27/FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance, but throughput growth of 30-40% YoY is the usual target. FY27 capex is USD1.2 billion and FY28 is about INR5,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: JNPT expansion timing and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning starts around next month, with most capacity running by H1 and completion around October; realisations are expected to be strong from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kandla-Gorakhpur, Mangalore-Hassan and Uran-Chakan pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Kandla-Gorakhpur connects in H1 FY27; Uran-Chakan is about a million tons; Mangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli is expected in FY28, with the Mangalore LPG rail gantry earlier.

risks_watch: Capex execution at scale: USD5 billion by 2030, with 12 ports targeted from seven, and funding that relies on a second-phase QIP and debt at about 0.6x gearing.
LPG import disruption from the Strait of Hormuz conflict; management expects normalisation from Q2 FY27.
Timing of JNPT Phase 1 (Q1 FY27), CRL4 at Kandla (FY27), Pipavav VLGC jetty and ammonia terminal commissioning, and the Pipavav petroleum product operations by year-end.

Ammonia business is early-stage; Pipavav ammonia terminal is about one-third contracted to Hindustan Zinc, with ITOCHU holding 10% of the ammonia subsidiary and planning to raise it to 25% over three years.
Vadhvan port project (about INR20,000 crores outlay) is only a non-binding MoU, subject to approvals and land allocation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and capex, with a clear long-term plan. Management was more hedged on specifics: no formal guidance, FY28 capex still to be finalised, and several timelines (Kochi, Mangalore, Vadhvan, Bangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli) left open.
key_quotes: We always follow demand, we are not somebody who will do flag planting and do anything prematurely.
Now we are doing it at a pace of, let's say, INR4,000 crores or INR5,000 crores a year.
So, being vertically integrated in LPG business helps Aegis Vopak as well as Aegis Logistics and the Group as a whole to get over this situation.

growth.why: Management reiterated 30-40% FY27 throughput growth (described as a standing target, not formal guidance), backed by the JNPT liquid expansion (318,100 CBM, due to start contributing from Q2 FY27), Kandla CRL4, Pipavav ammonia and LPG jetty, but the brief gives no volume or order-book bridge to the growth figure.
